H1.body:
a The first letter of the Nāgarī Alphabet.
— aH [avati, atati sAtatvena tizWatIti vA; av-at vA, qa Tv.]
1
N. of Viṣṇu, the first of the three sounds constituting the sacred syllable om; akAro vizRuruddizwa ukArastu maheSvaraH . makArastu smfto brahmA praRavastu trayAtmakaH ..; for more explanation of the three syllables a, u, m see om.
2
N. of Śiva, Brahmā, Vāyu, or Vaiśvānara.
—
ind.
1 A prefix corresponding to Latin in,
Eng. in or un,
Gr. a or an, and joined to nouns, adjectives, indeclinables (or even to verbs) as a substitute for the negative particle naY, and changed to an before vowels except in the word a-fRin. The senses of na usually enumerated are six- (a) sAdfSya ‘likeness’ or ‘resemblance’; abrAhmaRaH one like a Brāhmaṇa (wearing the sacred thread &c.), but not a Brāhmaṇa, but a Kṣatriya, or Vaiśya; anikzu : a reed appearing like ikzu, but not a true ikzu. (b) aBAva ‘absence’, ‘negation’, ‘want’, ‘privation’; ajYAnaM absence of knowledge, ignorance; akroDaH, anaMgaH, akaMwakaH, aGawaH &c. (c) Beda ‘difference’ or ‘distinction’; apawaH not a cloth, something different from, or other than, a cloth. (d) alpatA ‘smallness’, ‘diminution’, used as a diminutive particle; anudarA having a slender waist (kfSodarI or tanumaDyamA). (e) aprASastya ‘badness,’ ‘unfitness,’ having a depreciative sense; akAlaH wrong or improper time; akAryaM not fit to be done, improper, unworthy, bad act. (f) viroDa ‘opposition’, ‘contrariety’; anItiH the opposite of morality, immorality; asita not
(
pb) white, black; asura not a god, a demon &c. These senses are put together in the following verse: -tatsAdfSyamaBAvaSca tadanyatvaM tadalpatA . aprASastyaM viroDaSca naYarTAH zaw prakIrtitAH .. See na also. With verbal derivatives, such as gerunds, infinitives, participles, it has usually the sense of ‘not’; adagDvA not having burnt: apaSyan not seeing; so asakft not once; amfzA, akasmAt &c. Sometimes a does not affect the sense of the second member; a-paScima that which has no last,
i. e. last; anuttama having no superior, unsurpassed, most excellent; for examples see the words.
2 An interjection of (a) Pity (ah!) a avadyaM P. I. 1. 14 Sk. (b) Reproach, censure (fie, shame); apacasi tvaM jAlma P. VI. 3. 73
Vārt. See akaraRi, ajIvani also. (c) Used in addressing; a anaMta. (d) It is also used as a particle of prohibition.
3 The augment prefixed to the root in the formation of the Imperfect, Aorist and Conditional Tenses.
N-B. -The application of this privative prefix is practically unlimited; to give every possible case would almost amount to a dictionary itself. No attempt will, therefore, be made to give every possible combination of this prefix with a following word; only such words as require a special explanation, or such as most frequently occur in the literature and enter into compounds, with other words, will be given; others will be found self-explaining when the English ‘in,’ ‘un,’ or ‘not,’ is substituted for a or an before the meaning of the second word, or the sense may be expressed by ‘less,’ ‘free from,’ ‘devoid or destitute of’ &c; akaTya unspeakable; adarpa without pride, or freedom from pride; apragalBa not bold; aBaga unfortunate; avitta
(
pb) destitute of wealth &c. &c. In many cases such compounds will be found explained under the second member. Most compounds beginning with a or an are either Tatpuruṣa or Bahuvrīhi (to be determined by the sense) and should be so dissolved.

afRin
a. (f being regarded as a consonant) Not a debtor, free from debt; divasasyAzwame BAge SAkaM pacati yo naraH . afRI cApravAsI ca sa vAricara modate .. Mb. The form anfRin also occurs in this sense.

aMS 10
U. aMSayati-te To divide, distribute, share among; also aMSApayati in this sense.

aMSaH [aMS ac]
1 A share, part, portion, division; member; sakfdaMSo nipatati Ms. 9. 47; turyAMSaH a fourth part; zazWa°; mamEvAMSo jIvaloke jIvaBUtaH sanAtanaH Bg. 15. 7; BuvamaMSAviva DarmayorgatO R. 8. 16; aMSena darSitAnukUlatA K. 159 partly.
2 A share in property, inheritance; svatoMSataH Ms. 8. 408; anaMSO klIbapatitO 9. 201; patnyaH kAryAH samAMSikAH Y. 2. 115.
3 The numerator of a fraction; anyonyahArABihatO harAMSO Līlā.; sometimes used for fraction itself.
4 A degree of latitude (or longitude); akzasyAMSAH samAKyAtAH zazwyuttaraSatatrayam; sa ca aMSaH zazwikalAtmakaH, kalA tu zazwivikalAtmikA.
5 The shoulder (more generally written aMsa,
q. v.).
6
N. of one of the Ādityas. The senses of ‘party’, ‘a share of booty,’ ‘earnest money’, which are said to occur in the Veda are traceable to 1. above.
Comp.
— aMSaH [za. ta.] a secondary incarnation; part of a portion.
— aMSi
adv. share by share.
— avatAraH
— taraRaM [za. ta.] descent (on earth) of parts of deities, partial
(
pb) incarnation; °tAra iva Darmasya Dk. 153; °ramiva kftAMtasya K. 31; uccEHSravasaH 79; so aMSAvatIrRamiva 108;
N. of Adhyāyas 64-67 of Ādiparvan of Bhārata.
— BAj,
— hara, -hArin
m.
f. [upa. samAsa] one who takes or has a share, one entitled to a share in the ancestral property, an heir, a coheir; piMqadoMSaharaScEzAM pUrvABAve paraH paraH Y. 2. 132; jAtopi dAsyAM SUdreRa kAmatoMSaharo Bavet 133.
— vivartin
a. [sa. ta.] slightly turned away, or turned away towards the shoulder; muKamaMSavivarti pakzmalAkzyAH Ś. 3. 26
v. l. for aMsavivarti.
— savarRanaM [za. ta.] reduction of fractions to the same denominator (atulyacCedayo rASyoH samacCedakaraRaM) anyonyahArABihatO harAMSO rASyoH samacCedaviDAnamevam Līlā.
— svaraH the keynote.

aMSakaH [aMS-Rvul; aMSikA
f.]
1 One having a share, a coheir, relative.
2 (svArTe kan) A share, portion, division; triMSAMSakastaTA rASerBAgEtyaBiDIyate; dviBartfkA mezanavAMSake syAt, vfzAMSake sA paSuSIlayuktA.
— kaM A solar day.

aMSala
a. [aMSaM lAti; lA-ka]
1 Having, or entitled to, a share (aMSagrAhaka).
2 aMsala,
q. v.
aMSanaM [aMS-lyuw] Act of dividing.

aMSayitf
m. (aMS-tfc) A divider, sharer.

aMSin
a. [aMSa-ini]
1 A sharer, coheir; (punarviBAgakaraRe) sarve vA syuH samAMSinaH Y. 2. 114 entitled to the same share.
2 Having parts or members (avayavin); aMSinaH svAMSagAtyaMtABAvaM prati mfzAtmatAM - V. Paribhāṣā.

aMSya
a. [aMS-karmaRi yat] Divisible.

aMSuH [aMS-mfga° ku.]
1 A ray, beam of light; caMqa°, Garma° hot-rayed, the sun; sUryAMSuBirBinnamivAraviMdaM Ku. 1. 32; lustre, brilliance; ratna°, naKa° &c.
2 A point or end.
3 A small or minute particle.
4 End of a thread.
5 A filament, especially of the Soma plant (
Ved.)
6 Garment; decoration.
7
N. of a sage or of a prince.
8 Speed, velocity (vega).
Comp.
— jAlaM a collection of rays, a blaze or halo of light.
— DaraH,
— patiH -Bft, -bARaH-Bartf.
— svAmI the sun, (bearer of rays or lord of rays).
— pawwaM a kind of silken cloth (aMSunA sUkzmasUtreRa yuktaM pawwaM) Y. 1. 186, Ms. 5. 120.
— mAlA a garland of light, halo.
— mAlin
m. [aMSavaH mAleva, tataH astyarTe ini]
1 the sun (wreathed with, surrounded by, rays).
2 the number twelve.
3 having a collection of rays.
— hastaH [aMSuH hasta iva yasya] the sun (who draws up water from the earth by
(
pb) means of his 1000 hands in the form of rays).

aMSumat
a. [aMSu-astyarTe matup]
1 Luminous, radiant; jyotizAM raviraMSumAn Bg. 10. 21.
2 Pointed.
3 Fibrous, abounding in filaments (
Ved.).
—
m. (mAn)
1 The sun; vAlaKilyErivAMSumAn R. 15. 10, Ki. 11. 6, Y. 3. 144; sometimes the moon also.
2
N. of the grandson of Sagara, son of Asamañjasa and father of Dilīpa.
3
N. of a mountain; °matPalA
N. of a plant kadalI Musa Sapientum or Paradisiaca.
— tI
1
N. of a plant sAlaparRI (
Mar. qavalA, sAlavaRa) Hedysarum Gangeticum.
2
N. of the river Yamunā.

aMSukaM [aMSavaH sUtrARi vizayo yasya; aMSu fSyAdi° ka]
1 A cloth, garment in general; stana° a breastcloth; sitAMSukA V. 3. 12; yatrAMSukAkzepavilajjitAnAM Ku. 1. 14; cInAMSukamiva ketoH Ś. 1. 34.
2 A fine or white cloth; Dunvan kalpadrumakisalayAnyaMSukAnIva vAtEH Me. 62; usually silken or muslin.
3 An upper garment; a mantle; also an under garment; kararudDanIvigaladaMSukAH striyaH Śi. 13. 31.
4 A leaf.
5 Mild or gentle blaze of light (nAtidIpti) (kaH also; svArTekas.).

aMSula
a. Radiant, luminous.
— laH [aMSuM praBAM budDipratiBAM lAti, lA-ka]
N. of the sage Cāṇakya; of any sage.
aMs aMsayati, aMsApayati See aMS.

aMsaH [aMs karmaBAvAdO ac]
1 A part, portion; See aMSa.
2 The shoulder, shoulder-blade.
3
N. of a Prince. (
— sO) The two angles of an altar. [
cf.
Goth. amsa;
L. ansa, humerus;
Gr. asilla.]
Comp.
— kUwaH [aMsaH kUwa iva bfhattvAt] a bull's hump, the protuberance between the shoulders; rAjanyoccAMsakUwakraTanapawurawadGoraDAraH kuWAraH Prab. 1. 7
— traM [upa. sa.]
1 an armour to protect the shoulders.
2 a bow.
— PalakaH the upper part of the spine.
— BAraH (aMse°) [aMse Dfto BAraH SAka. ta. vA aluk] a burden or yoke put upon the shoulder.
— BArika,
— BArin
a. (aMse°) [BastrAdi gaRa, aMsa (se) BAreRa harati; zWan] bearing a yoke or burden on the shoulder.
— vivartin
a. [upa. sa.] turned towards the shoulders; muKamaMsavivarti pakzmalAkzyAH Ś. 3. 26.

aMsala
a. [aMsa lac, balavati ityarTe; P. V. 2. 98] Strong, lusty, powerful, having strong shoulders; yuvA yugavyAyatabAhuraMsalaH R. 3. 34; Bujena upEtu yogaM punaraMsalena 16. 84; °puruzaprayatnaduScalaM Dk. 169.

aMsya
a. [aMse BavaH aMsa-yat.] Belonging to the shoulder; ye aMsyA ye aMgyAH sUcikAH Rv. 1. 191. 7.

aMh 1
A. aMhate, aMhituM To go; approach; set out, Bk. 3. 25, 46; 14. 51, 4. 4. &c.
—
Caus.
1 To send; tamAMjihanmETilayajYaBUmiM Bk. 2. 40, 15. 75.
2 To shine.
3 To speak.

aMhura
a. [aMhf-madgurAdi urac] Moving (gatiyukta); Rv. 10. 5. 6; distressed, straitened, sinful (?).

aMhUraRa
a.
Ved. distressing, troublesome; sinful; straitened.
— RaM A sin, distress (?).

aMhoyu
a. Troublesome, free from sin (?).

aMhatiH
— tI
f. [han-ati, aMhAdeSaSca; haMteratiH syAdaMhAdeSaSca DAtoH Uṇ. 4. 62; haMti duritamanayA dAnaM]
1 A gift.
2 Anxiety, trouble, care, distress, illness (
Ved.)

aMhas
n. aMhaH -hasI &c. [am asun hukaca Uṇ. 4. 212, amati gacCati prAyaScittena]
1 A sin; sahasA saMhatimaMhasAM vihaMtuM … alaM Ki. 5. 17; kftaH kftArTosmi nibarhitAMhasA Śi. 1. 29; leaving one's religion or duty (svaDarmatyAga).
2 Trouble, anxiety, care. [
cf. aGa, Agas;
Gr. agos; ahos]. °muc
a. freeing from distress.

aMhasaspatiH
Ved. The intercalary month (lord of distress or perplexity?)

aMhasvat
a. Sinful.

aMhitiH
— tI
f. [aMh ktin grahAditvAt iw Tv.] A gift.

aMhu
a. [aMh mfga° ku]
Ved. Sinful, wicked, injurious (pApakArin, hananaSIla;) strait, narrow (?)
— hu
n.
1 Anxiety, distress; sin, crime (?).
2 Pudendum Muliebre (?). [
cf.
L. angustus, anxius;
Goth. aggvus].
— Beda -dI having a narrow slit; having the pudendum divided (?).

aMhriH [aMh vaMkryAdi krin, aMhate gacCatyanena]
1 A foot.
2 The root of a tree,
cf. aMGri.
3 The number four.
Comp.
— paH ‘foot-drinker’, a tree; (mUlena pibati siktatoyaM).
— skaMDaH [aMhreH skaMDa iva] the upper part of the sole of the foot.

ak 1
P. (akati) To go, move tortuously like a serpent [
cf.
L. angulus,
Gr. agkai].

aka
a. Moving tortuously.
akaM [na kaM suKaM] Absence of happiness; pain, misery; (as in nAka na akaM duHKaM yatra;) sin nAsti kaM suKaM yasmAt.

akaca
a. [na. ba.] Bald.
— caH
N. of Ketu (the descending node), who
(
pb) is represented as a headless trunk. Tv. explains it thus: akAya duHKAya cAyate; cAy-qa; ketugrahasya udayena lokopaplavasya SAstraprasidDiH;
e. g. upaplavAya lokAnAM DUmaketurivotTitaH Ku. 2. 32.

akaqamaM, akaTahaM, °cakraM
N. of a mystical circle (cakra) or diagram with the letters of the alphabet, such as a, ka, qa, ma, a, ka, Ta, ha &c. written therein and used in determining the auspicious or inauspicious stars of a person; (grAhyagopAlamaMtrasya- taMtroktamaMtragrahaRArTaM-tattanmaMtrARAM SuBASuBavicAropayogI cakraBedaH Tv.)

akaTita
a. ‘Not told,’ not otherwise mentioned by way of any of the other case-relations, such as apAdAna &c; a name given to the indirect (gORa) object governed by verbs like duh, yAc &c.

akanizWa
a. Not the youngest (such as eldest, middle); elder, superior.
— zWaH [ake vedaniMdArUpe pApe nizWA yasya saH]
N. of Buddha Gautama; of a deified Buddhist saint (
pl. in this latter sense.)
Comp.
— paH (gaH also) [akanizWAn budDAn pAtIti; pA-ka.]
N. of Buddha, lord of Buddhists.
akanyA [na. ta.] No virgin, a maid that is not so any longer; akanyeti tuyaH kanyAM brUyAt dvezeRa mAnavaH Ms. 8. 225. 6.

akaMpana
a. [na. ta.] Not shaking.
— naH
N. of a Rākṣasa.

akaMpita
a. [na. ta.] Unshaken, firm, resolute; not tremulous.
— taH
N. of a Jaina or Buddha saint, a pupil of the last Tīrthaṃkara (kaMpitaM budDivftteScAlanaM tannAsti yasya).

akara
a. [na. ba.]
1 Handless, maimed.
2 Exempt from tax or duty.
3 [na. ta.] Not doing or acting; not disposed to work, ceasing from work.
— rA
N. of a plant AmalakI, Emblic Myrobalan, Phyllanthus Emblica (akaM duHKaM sevanAt lokAnAM rAti gfhRAti nASayatIti; rA-ka Tv.)

akaraRaM [kf-BAve lyuw na. ta.] Not doing, absence of action; akaraRAt maMdakaraRaM SreyaH;
cf. the English phrases “Something is better than nothing,” “Better late than never”.
— Ra
a. [na. ba.]
1 Not artificial, natural.
2 Devoid of all organs, epithet of the Supreme Spirit.

akaraRiH
f. [naY-kf-AkroSe aniH; AkroSe naYi aniH P. III. 3. 112.] Failure, disappointment, non-accomplishment, mostly used in
(
pb) imprecations; tasyAkaraRirevAstu Sk. may he be disappointed, or experience a failure!

akarRa
a. [nAsti karRo yasya]
1 Devoid of ears; deaf.
2 Destitute of Karṇa; anarjunamakarRaM vAjagadadyeti niScitaH Mb.
— rRaH A serpent (tasya cakzuzEva SravaRAt, hence also called cakzuHSravAH)

akarRya
a. [na. ta.] Not fit for the ears; not in the ears.

akartana
a. [kft-BAve lyuw na. ta.]
1 Not cutting.
2 [kft-yuc na. ba.; uccasTaM PalaM kartituM SIlamasya Tv.] Dwarfish.

akartf
m. [na. ta.] Not an agent; akartari ca kArake P. III. 3. 19; puruzo'kartA BoktA Sāṅkhya; a subordinate agent; °tvaM-tA an inferior or subordinate position.

akarman
a. [na. ba.]
1 Without work, idle; inefficient.
2 Disqualified for performing the necessary rites, wicked, degraded; akarmA dasyuraBi no Rv. 10. 22. 8.
3 (Gram.) Intransitive, generally in this sense akarmaka.
—
n. (rma).
1 Absence of work; absence of necessary observances; neglect of essential observances; inaction; karmaRo hyapi bodDavyaM bodDavyaM ca vikarmaRaH . akarmaRaSca bodDavyaM gahanA karmaRo gatiH Bg. 4. 17, 18.
2 An improper act; crime, sin.
Comp.
— anvita
a.
1 unengaged, unoccupied, idle.
2 criminal.
— kft
a. free from action, or doing an improper act.
— BogaH
1 enjoyment of freedom from the fruits of action.
2 renunciation of self-righteousness.
— SIla
a. lazy, indolent.

akarmaka
a. [nAsti karma yasya ba. kap] Intransitive; PalavyApArayorekanizWatAyAmakarmakaH Bhartṛhari; (
f.) akarmikA; prasidDeravivakzAtaH karmaRo'karmikA kriyA
ibid.

akarmaRya
a. [na. ta.]
1 Unable to work, inefficient, unfit for work.
2 Unfit to be done.

akala
a. [nAsti kalA avayavo yasya] Not in parts, without parts, epithet of the Supreme Spirit.

akalka
a. [nAsti kalko yatra]
1 Free from sediment, pure.
2 Sinless.
— lkA Moonlight.
akalkatA Honesty, integrity.

akalkana -ka
a. [nAsti kalkanaM daMBaH, kalko vA yasmin] Free from pride, humble, modest; honest.

akalpa
a. [na. ba.]
1 Uncontrolled, not subject to control or rules, unrestrained, unfettered.
2 Weak, unable.
3 Incomparable.

akalpita
a. [na. ta.] Not artificial or manufactured; natural, genuine.

akalya
a. [kalAsu sADuH kalyaH nirAmayaH na. ta.]
1 Unwell, ill, indisposed.
2 [kalyate iti kal-yat kalyaM miTyABUtaM; na. ta.] True; (taM) anInayadakalyasaMDo baMDanAgAraM Dk. 31.

akalyARa
a. [na. ta.] Inauspicious, unlucky.
— RaM Inauspiciousness, ill, evil, adversity.

akava -vA
a. [na kavyate varRyate; kav-A na. ta.] Indescribable (avarRanIya); not contemptible, not bad; °ariH = kutsitA arayo yasya sa kavAriH; na kavAriH a°; or yasya SatravopyakutsitA vftrAdayaH; or akutsitaM iyati ESvaryaM prApnoti.

akavi
a.
Ved. Unwise, foolish.

akasmAt
ind. [na kasmAt kiMcitkAraRADInatvaM yatra aluk sa.]
1 Accidentally, suddenly, unexpectedly, all of a sudden; akasmAdAgaMtunA saha viSvAso na yuktaH H. 1 coming by chance, an accidental visitor.
2 Without cause or ground, causelessly, in vain; nAkasmAt SAMqilI mAtA vikrIRAti tilEstilAn Pt. 2. 65; °deva BartfdvezyatAM gatAsi Dk. 135; nAkasmAdapriyaM vadet Y. 1. 132; aTa nu ripurakasmAd dvezwi naH putraBAMqe Mv. 2. 44; kaTaM tvAM tyajedakasmAtpatirAryavfttaH R. 14. 55, 73.

akAMqa
a. [nAsti kAMqaM avasaraH ucitakAlaH yasya]
1 Accidental, untoward, unexpected, sudden; akAMqapAMquraGanaprasparDi Mv. 5. 39 out of season; punarakAMqavivartanadAruRaH U. 4. 15; °pracaMqakalahayoH U. 6; patatu SirasyakAMqayamadaMqa ivEza BujaH Māl. 5. 31; °BaMguratAM saMsArasuKAnAM K. 172.
2 Destitute of stem or stock.
Comp.
— jAta
a. Suddenly born or produced.
— pAtaH unexpected occurrence; °upanatA kaM na lakzmIrvimohayet Ks. 5. 2.
— pAtajAta
a. dying as soon as born; perishing soon after birth H. 4. 83.
— SUlaM a sudden attack of colic.

akAMqe
adv. Unexpectedly, all of a sudden, suddenly; darBAMkureRa caraRaH kzata ityakAMqe tanvI sTitA katicideva padAni gatvA Ś. 2. 12; lajjAM vijitya vinayaM vinivArya DEryamunmaTya maTaMravivekamakAMqa eva Māl. 1. 18 unexpectedly; tAtastu tamakAMqa eva prARaharamapratikAramupaplavamAlokya K. 33.

akAma
a. [nAsti kAmo yasya]
1 Free from desire, affection, love; akAmasya kriyA kAciddfSyate neha karhicit Ms. 2. 4 every thing is an act of his will.
2 Reluctant, unwilling; °mAM kanyAM 4. 364; so nAkAmo dAtumarhati.
3
(
pb) Uninfluenced by, not subject to, love; BayAdakAmApi hi dfzwiviBramaM Ś. 1. 23.
4 Unconscious, unintentional; akAmopanateneva sADorhfdayamenasA R. 10. 39 unconsciously committed.
5 The Saṃdhi which causes the dropping of a final r before a following r.
Comp.
— karSana
a.
Ved. not frustrating desires.
— hata
a. not smitten with desire or affection, free from desire, calm.

akAmataH
adv. [akAma-paMcamyAstasil] Unwillingly, reluctantly, unintentionally, unconsciously; itare kftavaMtastu pApAnyetAnyakAmataH Ms. 9. 242; akAmataH kftaM pApaM vedAByAsena SuDyati 11. 46, 45.
akAmatA Absence of desire; na cEvehAstyakAmatA Ms. 2. 2.

akAya
a. [nAsti kAyo yasya]
1 Without body, incorporeal.
2 An epithet of Rāhu, who is represented as having no body, but only a head.
3 Epithet of the Supreme Spirit (without body, parts &c.)

akAra
a. [karotIti kAraH kf-GaY aR vA na. ta.] Not doing or acting, void of action (kriyArahita).
— raH The letter a; akzarARAmakArosmi Bg. 10. 33.

akAraRa
a. [na. ba.] Causeless, groundless, spontaneous; °mitrARi satAM cetAMsi K. 37 disinterested friends; IdfSo mAM pratyamIzAM °snehaH U. 6.
— RaM Absence of a cause, motive, or ground; akAraRAt parityajya K. 167 causelessly, without cause or ground; kimakAraRameva darSanaM vilapaMtyE rataye na dIyate Ku. 4. 7; °parityaktA mAtApitrorgurostaTA Ms. 3. 157; akAraRAt-raRaM-Re causelessly, in vain; tyakto vA syAdakAraRAt Ms. 9. 177; kimakAraRe kupyAsi, akAraRe AtmAnamAyAsayasi Ratn. 2 in vain.

akArRavezwakika
a. Not adapted for ear-rings (P. VI. 2. 155).

akArpaRya
a. [na. ba.] Got without meanness; akArpaRyamaSanaM Bh. 3. 51.

akArya
a. [na. ta.] Improper, not fit to be done.
— ryaM An improper, unworthy or bad act, a criminal or sinful action; mA nAma vEklavyAdakAryaM kuryAt Mk. 3 (AtmaGAtAdirUpaM).
Comp.
— kArin
a.
1 an evil-doer, one who commits a misdeed; mahApAtakinaScEva SezAScAkAryakAriRaH Ms. 11. 240.
2 one that neglects one's duty; dAnenAkAryakAriRaH (SuDyaMti) 5. 107.

akAla

In the Ṛgveda he and Vasiṣṭha are said to be the off-spring of Mitra and Varuṇa, whose seed fell from them at the sight of the lovely nymph Urvaśī at a sacrificial session. Part of the seed fell into a jar and part into water; from the former arose Agastya who is, therefore, called Kumbhayoni, Kumbhajanman, Ghaṭodbhava,
(
pb) Kalaśayoni &c.; from the latter Vasiṣṭha. From his parentage Agastya is also called Maitrāvaruṇi, Aurvaśeya, and, as he was very small when he was born, he is also called Mānya. He is represented to have humbled the Vindhya mountains by making them prostrate themselves before him when they tried to rise higher and higher till they wellnigh occupied the sun's disc and obstructed his path, See Vindhya. (This fable is supposed by some to typify the progress of the Āryas towards the south in their conquest and civilization of India, the humbling of the mountain standing metaphorically for the removal of physical obstacles in their way). He is also known by the names of Pītābdhi, Samudra-culuka &c., from another fable according to which he drank up the ocean because it had offended him and because he wished to help Indra and the gods in their wars with a class of demons called Kāleyas who had hid themselves in the waters and oppressed the three worlds in various ways. His wife was Lopāmudrā. She was also called Kauṣītakī and Varapradā. She bore him two sons, Dṛḍhāsya and Dṛḍhasyu. In the Rāmāyaṇa Agastya plays a distinguished part. He dwelt in a hermitage on mount Kuñjara to the south of the Vindhya and was chief of the hermits of the south. He kept under control the evil spirits who infested the south and a legend relates how he once ate up a Rākṣasa named Vātāpi, who had assumed the form of a ram, and destroyed by a flash of his eye the Rākṣasa's brother who attempted to avenge him. In the course of his wanderings Rāma with his wife and brother came to the hermitage of Agastya who received him with the greatest kindness and became his friend, adviser and protector. He gave Rāma the bow of Viṣṇu and accompanied him to Ayodhyā when he was restored to his kingdom after his exile of 14 years. The superhuman power which the sage possessed is also represented by another legend, according to which he turned king Nahuṣa into a serpent and afterwards restored him to his proper form. In the south he is usually regarded as the first teacher of science and literature to the primitive Dravidian tribes, and his era is placed by Dr. Caldwell in the 7th or 6th century
B. C. The Purāṇas represent Agastya as the son of Pulastya (the sage from whom the Rākṣasas sprang) and Havirbhuvā the daughter of Kardama. Several ‘hymn-seers’ are mentioned in his family, such as his two sons, Indrabāhu, Mayobhuva and Mahendra, also others who served to perpetuate the family. The sage is represented as a great philosopher, benevolent and kind-hearted, unsurpassed in the science of archery and to have taken a principal part in the colonization of the south; nirjitAsi mayA Badre SatruhastAdamarziRA . agastyena durADarzA muninA dakziReva dik .. Rām.; agastyAcaritAmASAM
(
pb) R. 4. 44;
cf. also: agastyo dakziRAmASAmASritya naBasi sTitaH . varuRasyAtmajo yogI viMDyavAtApimardanaH .. and R. 6. 61, Mv. 7. 14.]

L. ignis.] [Agni is the God of Fire, the Ignis of the Latins and Ogni of the Slavonians. He is one of the most prominent deities of the Ṛgveda. He is an immortal, has taken up his abode among mortals as their guest; he is the domestic priest, the successful accomplisher and protector of all ceremonies; he is also the religious leader and preceptor of the gods, a swift messenger employed to announce to the immortals the hymns and to convey to them the oblations of their worshippers, and to bring them down from the sky to the place of sacrifice. He is sometimes regarded as the mouth and the tongue through which both gods and men participate in the sacrifices. He is the lord, protector and leader of people, monarch of men, the lord of the house, friendly to mankind, and like a father, mother, brother &c. He is represented as being produced by the attrition of two pieces of fuel which are regarded as husband and wife. Sometimes he is considered to have been brought down from heaven or generated by Indra between two clouds or stones, created by Dyau, or fashioned by the gods collectively. In some passages he is represented as having a triple existence, which may mean his three-fold manifestations as the sun in heaven, lightning in the atmosphere, and as ordinary fire on the earth, although the three appearances are also elsewhere otherwise explained. His epithets are numberless and for the most part descriptive of his physical characteristics: DUmaketu, hutaBuj, Suci, rohitASva, saptajihva, tomaraDara, GftAnna, citraBAnu, UrDvaSocis, SocizkeSa, harikeSa, hiraRyadaMta, ayodaMzwra &c. In a celebrated passage he is said to have
4 horns,
3 feet,
2 heads, and
7 hands. The highest divine functions are ascribed to Agni. He is said to have spread out the two worlds and produced them, to have supported heaven, formed the mundane regions and luminaries of heaven, to have begotten Mitra and caused the sun to ascend the sky. He is the head and summit of the sky, the centre of the earth. Earth, Heaven and all beings obey his commands. He knows and sees all worlds or creatures and witnesses all
(
pb) their actions. The worshippers of Agni prosper, they are wealthy and live long. He is the protector of that man who takes care to bring him fuel. He gives him riches and no one can overcome him who sacrifices to this god. He confers, and is the guardian of, immortality. He is like a water-trough in a desert and all blessings issue from him. He is therefore constantly supplicated for all kinds of boons, riches, food, deliverance from enemies and demons, poverty, reproach, childlessness, hunger &c. Agni is also associated with Indra in different hymns and the two gods are said to be twin brothers.
Such is the Vedic conception of Agni; but in the course of mythological personifications he appears as the eldest son of Brahmā and is called Abhimānī (Vishṇu Purāṇa). His wife was Svāhā; by her he had
3 sons-Pāvaka, Pavamāna and Śuci; and these had forty-five sons: altogether 49 persons who are considered identical with the 49 fires. He is also represented as a son of Angiras, as a king of the Pitṛs or Manes, as a Marut and as a grandson of Śāṇḍila, and also as a star. The Harivaṃśa describes him as clothed in black, having smoke for his standard and head-piece and carrying a flaming javelin. He is borne in a chariot drawn by red horses and the 7 winds are the wheels of his car. He is accompanied by a ram and sometimes he is represented as riding on that animal. Agni was appointed by Brahmā as the sovereign of the quarter between the south and east, whence the direction is still known as Āgneyī. The Mahābhārata represents Agni as having exhausted his vigour and become dull by devouring many oblations at the several sacrifices made by king Śvetaki, but he recruited his strength by devouring the whole Khāṇḍava forest; for the story see the word KAMqava].

N. of a country and the people inhabiting it, the country about the modern Bhāgalpur in Bengal. [It lay on the south of Kauśikī Kaccha and on the right bank of the Ganges. Its capital was Campā, sometimes called Aṅgapurī, Lomapādapurī, Karṇapurī or Mālinī. According to Daṇḍin (aMgezu gaMgAtawe bahiScaMpAyAH) and Hiouen Thsang it stood on the Ganges about 24 miles west of a rocky island. General Cunningham has shown that this description applies to the hill opposite Pātharghātā, that it is 24 miles east of Bhāgalpur, and that there are villages called Champanagar and Champapura adjoining the last. According to Sanskrit poets the country of the Aṅgas lay to the east of Girivraja the capital of Magadha and to the north-east or south-east of Mithilā. The country

N. of a son of Vāli, monkey-king of Kishkindhā. [He was born of Tārā, Vālī's wife, and is supposed to have been an incarnation of Bṛhaspati to aid the cause of Rāma (and hence noted for his eloquence). When, after the abduction of Sītā by Rāvaṇa, Rāma sent monkeys in all quarters to search for her, Aṅgada was made chief of a monkey-troop proceeding to the south. For one month he got no information, and, when consequently he determined to cast off his life, he was told by Sampāti that Sītā could be found in Laṅkā. He sent Māruti to the island and, on the latter's return with definite information, they joined Rāma at Kiṣkindhā. Afterwards when the whole host of Rāma went to Laṅkā Aṅgada was despatched to Rāvaṇa as a messenger of peace to give him a chance of saving himself in time. But Rāvaṇa scornfully rejected his advice and met his doom. After Sugrīva Aṅgada became king of Kishkindhā. In common parlance a man
(
pb) is said to act the part of Aṅgada when he endeavours to mediate between two contending parties, but without any success.].

aMgiraH, aMgiras
m. [aMgati-aMgagatO asi iruw;] Uṇ. 4. 235; according to Ait. Br. aMgiras is from aMgAra; ye aMgArA AsaMsteMgiraso'Bavan; so Nir.; aMgArezu yobaBUva soMgirAH
N. of a celebrated sage to whom many hymns of the Ṛgveda are ascribed. Etymologically Aṅgiras is connected with the word Agni and is often regarded as its synonym (Sivo Bava prajAByo mAnuzIByastvamaMgiraH; aMgiroBiH fziBiH saMpAditatvAt aMgasOzWavAdvA aMgirA agnirUpaH). According to Bhārata he was a son of Agni. When Agni began to practise penance, Aṅgiras himself became Agni and surpassed him in power and lustre, seeing which Agni came to the sage and said: -nikzipAmyahamagnitvaM tvamagniH praTamo Bava . BavizyAmi dvitIyohaM prAjApatyaka eva ca .. Aṅgiras said: kuru puRyaM prajAsargaM BavAgnistimirApahaH . mAM ca deva kuruzvAgne praTamaM putramaMjasA .. tacCrutvAMgiraso vAkyaM jAtavedAstaTA'karot. He was one of the 10 mind-born sons of Brahmā. His wife was Śraddhā, daughter of Kardama and bore him
3 sons, Bṛhaspati, Utathya and Saṃvarta, and
4 daughters Kuhū, Sinīvālī, Rākā and Anumati. The Matsya Purāṇa says that Aṅgiras was one of the three sages produced from the sacrifice of Varuṇa and that he was adopted by Agni as his son and acted for some time as his regent. Another account, however, makes him father of Agni. He was one of the seven great sages and also one of the 10 Prajāpatis or progenitors of mankind. In latter times Aṅgiras was one of the inspired lawgivers, and also a writer on Astronomy. As an astronomical personification he is Bṛhaspati, regent of Jupiter or Jupiter itself. He is also regarded as the priest of the gods and the lord of sacrifices. Besides Śraddhā his wives were Smṛti, two daughters of Maitreya, some daughters of Dakṣa, Svadhā and Satī. He is also regarded as a teacher of the Brahmavidyā. The Vedic hymns are also said to be his daughters. According to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Aṅgiras begot sons possessing Brāhmanical glory on the wife of Rathītara, a Kṣatriya who was childless and these persons were afterwards called descendants of Aṅgiras. The principal authors of vedic hymns in the family of Angiras were 33. His family has three distinct branches kevalAMgirasa, gOtamAMgirasa and BAradvAjAMgirasa, each branch having a number of subdivisions. -(
pl.)

(
pb) objects, and at a later period they became for the most part personifications of light, of luminous bodies, of divisions of time, celestial phenomena and fires adapted to peculiar occasions, as the full moon and change of the moon, or to particular rites, as the aSvameDa, rAjasUya &c.]
2 Hymns of the Atharvaveda.
3 Priests, who, by using magical formulas of the Atharvaveda, protect the sacrifice against the effects of inauspicious accidents.

9 (naM nA) (
Rhet.) A suggested meaning; also the process by which such meaning is suggested. It is the power of suggestion (founded on aBiDA or lakzaRA denotation or indication), by which something else is understood from a word which, though having more meanings than one, has been restricted to a single meaning by relations of conjunction, disjunction &c. (saMyoga, viprayoga, sAhacarya, viroDitA &c.), or, briefly, the use of a word of several meanings in a special sense determined by the context;

aMjanA
1
N. of the female elephant of the north.
2
N. of the mother of Māruti or Hanūmat. [She was the daughter of a monkey named Kunjara and wife of Kesarin, another monkey. She was in a former birth a celestial nymph by name Puñjikasthalī and was born on earth owing to a curse. One day while she was seated on the summit of a mountain, her garment was slightly displaced, and the God of Wind being enamoured of her beauty assumed a visible form, and asked her to yield to his desires. She requested him not to violate her chastity, to which he consented; but he told her that she would conceive a son equal to himself in strength and lustre by virtue of his amorous desire fixed on her, and then disappeared. In course of time Anjanā conceived and brought forth a son who
(
pb) was called Māruti being the son of Māruta.]

ind. [at-i]
1 A prefix used with adjectives and adverbs, meaning ‘very’, ‘too’, ‘exceedingly’, ‘excessively’, ‘very much,’ and showing utkarza; nAtidUre not very far from; °kfSa very lean; °BfSaM very much; also with verbs or verbal forms; °siktameva BavatA Sk.; svaBAvo hyatiricyate &c.
2 (With verbs) Over, beyond; ati-i go beyond, overstep; so °kram, °car, °vah &c. In this case ati is regarded as a preposition upasarga.
3 (a) (With nouns or pronouns) Beyond, past, surpassing, superior to, eminent, respectable, distinguished, higher, above, (used with
acc. as a karmapravacanIya, or as first member of
Bah. or
Tat. Comp.; in which last case it has usually the sense of eminence or higher degree: atigo, °gArgyaH, = praSastA gOH, SoBano, gArgyaH; °rAjan an excellent king; or the sense of atikrAMta must be understood with the latter member which will then stand in the accusative case; atimartyaH = martyamatikrAMtaH; °mAlaH, atikrAMto mAlAM; so atikAya, °keSara,
q. v.); ati devAn kfzRaH Sk.; mAnuzAnatigaMDarvAn sarvAngaMDarva lakzaye Mb; °mAnuzaM karma a deed
(
pb) which is beyond human power,
i. e. a superhuman action; °kaSaH past the whip (as a horse), unmanageable; °tyad surpassing that; °tvAM, °tvAn him or them that surpasses or surpass thee, so °mAM, °yUyaM &c. (b) (With nouns derived from roots) Extravagant, exaggerated, inordinate, excessive, extraordinary;
e. g. °AdaraH excessive regard; °ASA extravagant hope; so °BayaM, °tfzRA, °AnaMdaH &c. &c.; atidAnAt balirbadDo nazwo mAnAtsuyoDanaH . vinazwo rAvaRo lOlyAdati sarvatra varjayet;
cf. ‘extremes are ever bad.’ (c) Unfit, idle, improper, in the sense of asaMprati or kzepa ‘censure’; atinidraM = nidrA saMprati na yujyate Sk. The gaRaratnamahodaDi gives the following senses of atiH - vikramAtikramAbudDiBfSArTAtiSayezvati .
e. g. atiraTaH raTADikaM vikramavAn; °matiH budDyatikramaH; °gahanaM budDeravizayaH; °taptaM BfSataptaM; °vegaH atiSayito vegaH.

7 (Intrans.) To pass, elapse (time); atyeti rajanI yA tu sA na pratinivartate Rām.; atIte dakziRAyane &c.
8 To overflow, be redundant, be in excess.
9 To die.

atri

— triH
N. of a celebrated sage and author of many Vedic hymns. [He appears in the Vedas in hymns addressed to Agni, Indra, the Aśvins and the Viśvedevas. In the Svāyambhuva Manvantara he appears as one of the ten Prajāpatis or mind-born sons of Brahmā, being born from his eye. These sons having died by the curse of Śiva, Brahmā performed a sacrifice, at the beginning of the present Vaivasvata Manvantara, and Atri was born from the flames of Agni. Anasūyā was his wife in both lives. In the first she bore him three sons, Datta, Durvāsas and Soma; in the second she had two additional children, a son by name Aryaman and a daughter called Amalā. In the Rāmāyaṇa an account is given of the visit paid by Rāma and Sītā to Atri and Anasūyā in their hermitage, when they both received them most kindly; See Anasūyā. As a Ṛṣi or sage he is one of the seven sages who were all sons of Brahmā, and represents in Astronomy one of the stars of the Great Bear situated in the north. He is also the author of a code of laws known as atrismfti or atrisaMhitA. In the Purāṇas he is said to have produced the moon from his eye, while he was practising austere penance, the moon being in consequence called atrija, -jAta, -dfgja, atrinetraprasUta, -°praBava, °Bava &c.;
cf. also aTa nayanasamutTaM jyotiratreriva dyOH R. 2. 75 and atreriveMduH V. 5. 21.] -(
pl.) descendants of Atri.

(usually followed by iti at the end, iti praTamoMkaH here ends &c.).

oft. followed by tataH or taTApi, Bg. 12. 9, 11; 2. 26; aTa cet but if Bg. 2. 33; 18. 58.

cf. Mv. 2. 24 mUrtimaBirAmaGorAM biBradivATarvaRo nigamaH. It has nine Śākhās and five Kalpas, and is comprised in 20 Kāṇḍas. The most important Brāhmaṇa belonging to this Veda is the Gopatha-Brāhmaṇa, and the Upaniṣads pertaining to it are stated to be 52, or, according to another account, 31.] [

(
pb) Rv. 1. 89. 16 he interprets by taking aditi to mean adIna
i. e. anupakzIRa, na hyezAM kzayosti iti. In the Ṛgveda Aditi is frequently implored ‘for blessings on children and cattle, for protection and for forgiveness’. She is called ‘Devamātā’ being strangely enough represented both as mother and daughter of Dakṣa. She had
8 sons; she approached the gods with 7 and cast away the 8th (Mārtaṇḍa, the sun.) In another place Aditi is addressed as ‘supporter of the sky, sustainer of the earth, sovereign of this world, wife of Viṣṇu’, but in the Mahābhārata, Rāmāyaṇa and Purāṇas, Vishṇu is said to be the son of Aditi, one of the several daughters of Dakṣa and given in marriage to Kaśyapa by whom she was mother of Viṣṇu in his dwarf incarnation, and also of Indra, and she is called mother of gods and the gods her sons, ‘aditinandanas’; See Dakṣa and Kaśyapa also].

6 A topic, subject; section, article or paragraph; a complete argument treating of one subject; the Sūtras of Vyāsa and Jaimini are divided into Adhyāyas, the Adhyāyas into Pādas and the Pādas into Adhikaraṇas or sections. According to the Mīmāṃsakas a complete Adhikaraṇa consists of five members:
— vizaya the subject or matter to be explained, viSaya or saMSaya the doubt or question arising upon that matter, pUrvapakza the first side or prima facie argument concerning it, uttara or uttarapakza or sidDAMta the answer or demonstrated conclusion, and saMgati pertinency or relevancy, or (according to others nirRaya the final conclusion); vizayo viSayaScEva pUrvapakzastaTottaraM . nirRayaSceti sidDAMtaH SAstre' DikaraRaM smftam .. The Vedāntins put saMgati in the 3rd place, and sidDAMta last; tatra ekEkamaDikaraRaM paMcAvayavaM, vizayaH saMdehaH saMgatiH pUrvapakzaH sidDAMtaSca. Generally speaking, the five members may be taken to be vizaya, saMSaya, pUrvapakza, uttarapakza and sidDAMta or rAdDAMta.
7 Court of justice, court, tribunal; svAndozAn kaTayaMti nADikaraRe Mk. 9. 3; °raRe ca sADanaM Dk. 40.

loc.) aDItI caturzvAmnAyezu Dk. 120; vede, vyAkaraRe &c.; tvaguttarAsaMgavatImaDItinIM Ku. 5. 16 muttering holy prayers, engaged in repeating sacred texts.

aDIyAnaH
pres. p. A student, one who goes over the Vedas.

aDyayaH [i-BAve ac]
1 Learning, study; remembrance.
2 = aDyAya,
q. v.

aDyApakaH [aDi-i-Ric-Rvul] A teacher, preceptor, instructor; especially of the Vedas; vyAkaraRa°, nyAya° professor or teacher of grammar, logic &c.; Bftaka° a hired teacher, mercenary teacher; °uditaH styled a professor. According to Viṣṇu Smṛti an adhyāpaka is of
2 kinds: he is either an Ācārya
i. e. one who invests a boy with the sacred thread and initiates him into the Vedas, or he is an Upādhyāya
i. e. one who teaches for livelihood (vfttyarTaM) See Ms. 2. 140-141 and the two words.

aDyApanaM [i-Ric, BAve-lyuw] Teaching, instructing, lecturing, especially on sacred knowledge; one of the
(
pb) six duties of a Brāhmaṇa. According to Indian law-givers aDyApana is of three kinds: (1) undertaken for charity, (2) for wages and (3) in consideration of services rendered;
cf. Hārīta: aDyApanaM ca triviDaM DarmArTamfkTakAraRam . SuSrUzAkaraRaM ceti triviDaM parikIrtitam ..

aDyApayitf
m. [i-Ric-tfc] A teacher, instructor.

aDyAya
a. [i-GaY P. III. 3. 21] (At the end of
comp.) A reader, student, one who studies; vedADyAyaH a student of the Vedas; so maMtra°-yaH
1 Reading, learning, study, especially of the Vedas; praSAMtADyAyasatkaTA ( nagarI) Rām.
2 Proper time for reading or for a lesson; °jYAH pracakzate Ms. 4. 102, see anaDyAya also.
3 A lesson, lecture; aDIyate'smin aDyAyaH P. III. 3. 122; so svADyAyo'DyetavyaH
4 A chapter, a large division of a work, such as of the Rāmāyaṇa, Mahābhārata, Manu Smṛti, Pāṇini's Sūtras &c. The following are some of the names used by Sanskrit writers to denote chapters or divisions of works:
— sargo vargaH paricCedodGAtADyAyAMkasaMgrahAH . ucCvAsaH parivartaSca pawalaH kAMqamAnanaM . sTAnaM prakaraRaM cEva parvollAsAhnikAni ca . skaMDAMSO tu purARAdO prAyaSaH parikIrtitO ..

aDyAyin
a. [i-Rini] Studying.

aDyetf
m.,
— trI
f. A student, learner.

aDIkAraH [kf-GaY upasargadIrGatvaM] = aDikAra
q. v.; svAgataM svAnaDIkArAnabalaMbya Ku. 2. 18; Ms. 11. 64.

aDIna
a. [aDi-Ka P. V. 4. 7; aDigataH inaM praBuM vA] Subject to, subservient, dependent on; usually in
comp.; sTAne prARAH kAminAM dUtyaDInAH M. 3. 14; tvadaDInaM Kalu dehinAM suKaM Ku. 4. 10; ikzvAkURAM durApe'rTe tvadaDInA hi sidDayaH R. 1. 72; kena nimittena BavadaDIno jAtaH Dk. 7 consigned to your care.

aDImaMTa = aDimaMTa,
q. v.

aDIra
a.
1 Not bold, timid.
2 Confused, lacking self-command, excited, excitable.
3 Fitful, capricious.
4 Unsteady, not fixed, tremulous, rolling; °viprekzitamAyatAkzyA Ku. 1. 46; °locanaH Śi. 1. 53; 6. 25.
5 Querulous, foolish, weak-minded.
— rA
1 Lightning.
2 A capricious or quarrelsome mistress; see under nAyikA.
aDIvAsaH [vas AcCAdane karaRe GaY] A long coat or mantle covering the whole person (uparizwAdAvarakaM vAsaH).
aDISaH [aDikaH ISaH] Lord, supreme lord or master, sovereign ruler; aMga°, mfga°, manuja° &c.

aDISvaraH [aDikaH ISvaraH]
1 A supreme lord or an employer.
2 An Arhat (among Jainas).

aDIzwa
a. [aDi-iz divAdi-kta] Honorary, solicited.
— zwaH [BAve-kta] Honorary office or duty; one of the cases in which liN or the Potential may be used; P. III. 3. 161 (aDIzwaH = satkArapUrvako vyApAraH Sk.).

aDunA
ind. [asmin kAle; idamaH idaMSabdasya saptamyaMtAtkAlavAcinaH svArTe aDunApratyayaH syAt P. V. 3. 17 Sk.] Now, at this time; pramadAnAmaDunA viqaMbanA Ku. 4. 12.

aDunAtana
a. (nI
f.) [aDunA BavArTe wyul tuwca] Belonging to the present times, modern.

aDura
a. [nAsti DUH ciMtABAro vA yasya] Not laden, free from the burden of cares &c.
— DUH [na. ta.] Absence of burden or cares.
aDUmakaH [na. ba.] ‘Smokeless’, burning or blazing fire.

aDfta
a. Not held or controlled &c.
— taH One of the 1000 names of Viṣṇu (sarvezAM DArakatvena kenApi na DftaH svapratizWitaH parameSvaraH).

aDftiH
f.
1 Want of firmness or control, looseness.
2 Incontinence.
3 Unhappiness.

aDfzwa
a.
1 Not bold, modest, shy.
2 Invincible, irresistible; unhurt; hUtAso vasavo 'DfzwAH Rv. 6. 50. 4.

aDfzya
a.
1 Invincible, unassailable; manasApyaDfzyaM Ku. 3. 51 unassailable even in thought; unapproachable (
opp. aBigamya); aDfzyaScABigamyaSca yAdoratnErivArRavaH R. 1. 16.
2 Modest, shy.
3 Proud.
aDenuH [na. ta.] A cow not yielding milk.

aDErya
a. [na. ba.] Without selfpossession, courage &c., swayed by excitement.
— ryaM Absence of courage, firmness or control; excitability.
aDo'kza, aDoMSuka, aDo'kzaja See under aDas.

aDyakza
a. [aDigataH akzaM iMdriyaM vyavahAraM vA]
1 Perceptible to the senses, visible; yEraDyakzEraTa nijasaKaM nIradaM smArayadBiH Bv. 4. 17.
2 One who exercises supervision, presiding over.
— kzaH
(
pb)
1 A superintendent, president, head, lord, master, controller, ruler; mayA'DyakzeRa prakftiHsUyate sacarAcaraM Bg. 9. 10; yadaDyakzeRa jagatAM vayamAropitAstvayA Ku. 6. 17;
oft. in
comp.; gaja°, senA°, grAma°, dvAra°.
2 An eye-witness (
Ved.).
3
N. of a plant (kzIrikA) Mimusops Kauki.

aDyakzaraM
ind. On the subject of syllables; above all syllables.
— raM The mystic syllable om.

aDyagni
ind. [agnO agnisamIpe vA] Over, by or near the nuptial fire.
—
n. (gni) One of the six kinds of strIDana (woman's property) mentioned in Ms. 9. 194; a gift made to a woman at the time of marriage: vivAhakAle yatstrIByo dIyate hyagnisanniDO . tadaDyagnikftaM sadBiH strIDanaM parikIrtitam .. So aDyagnikftaM-aDyagnyupAgataM; pitfmAtfpatiBrAtfdattamaDyagnyupAgatam . ADivedanikAdyaM ca strIDanaM parikIrtitam.

aDyaMc [aDi-aMc-kvip]
1 Tending upwards; superior, eminent.
2 One who obtains or acquires.

aDyaMqA [aDikamaMqamiva bIjaM yasyAH sA]
N. of two plants (ajaSfMgI) Carpopogon Pruriens, and BUmyAmalakI Flacourtia Cataphracta.

aDyaDi
ind. On high (
acc.); °Di lokaM Sk.
aDyaDikzepaH [aDikaH aDikzepaH] Excessive abuse or censure, gross abuse; Y. 3. 228.

aDyaDIna
a. [ADikyena aDInaH] Completely subject or dependent, as a slave; nADyaDIno na vaktavyo na dasyurna vikarmakft . Ms. 8. 66 (Kull. atyaMtaparataMtro garBadAsaH).
aDyaya, aDyayanaM &c. See under aDI.

aDyarDa
a. [aDikamarDaM yasya] Having an additional half; ekADikaM harejjyezWaH putro'DyarDaM tato'nujaH Ms. 9. 117; SatamaDyarDamAyatA Mb.,
i. e. 150; °yojanaSatAt Pt. 2. 18. (In
comp. with a following noun) Amounting to or worth one and a half; °kaMsa amounting to one and a half Kaṃsa; so °kAkiRIka, kArzApaRa-Rika, °KArIka, °paRya, °pAdya, °pratika, °mAzya, °viMSatikIna, °Sata-tya, °Sa-SA-tamAna °SARa, °SARya, °SUrpa, °sahasra, °sOvarRa &c. (P. V. 1. 28-35.).
— rDaH Wind (yadasmin idaM sarvaM aDyArDnot aDikamavarDayat tena aDyarDaH pavanaH iti sTitam Bṛ. Up.).
aDyarbudaM [aDikaM or aDijAtaM arbudaM] A tumour, goitre; yajjAyate'nyatKalu pUrvajati jYeyaM tadaDyarbudamarbudajYEH Suśr.

aDyavaso 4
P.
1 To determine, resolve; kaTamidAnIM durjanavacanAdevaM aDyavasitaM devena U. 1; adurlaBaM maraRamaDyavasitaM K. 171; kimaDyavasyaMti guravaH Ve. 1; aBiDAtumaDyavasasO na girA Śi. 9. 76; resolve or mean to do.
2 To attempt, exert, undertake; mA sAhasaM aDyavasyaH Dk. 123; vrataM duzkaramaDyavasitaM H. 1.
3 To grapple with.
4 To conceive, apprehend, think; akAryaM kAryavadaDyavasya Dk. 86.

aDyavasAnaM [BAve-lyuw]
1 Effort, determination &c. See aDyavasAya.
2 (In
Rhet.) Identification of two things (prakfta and aprakfta) in such a manner that the one is completely absorbed into the other; nigIryADyavasAnaM tu prakftasya pareRa yat K. P. 10; on such identification is founded the figure called atiSayokti, and the lakzaRA called sADyavasAnA. See K. P. 2.

aDyavasAyaH
1 An attempt, effort, exertion; na svalpamapyaDyavasAyaBIroH karoti vijYAnaniDirguRaM hi H. 1.
v. l.; °sahacarezu sAhasezu Dk. 161.
2 Determination, resolution; mental effort or apprehension; saMBAvanaM nAma astitvADyavasAyaH P. VI. 2. 21.
3 Perseverance, diligence, energy, constancy; tatkoyaM pade pade mahAnanaDyavasAyaH U. 4 absence of energy or resolution, drooping of spirits; (with mahAnaDyavasAyaH as the reading, the meaning would be ‘why this effort on your part
i. e. to determine whether you should go or not, hesitation’.).

aDyavasAyin
a. [so-Rini] Attempting; resolute, persevering, energetic.

aDyavasita
p. p. Attempted, mentally apprehended, determined.
aDyavahananaM [aDi upari avahananaM] Beating again what is being threshed and peeled (pUrvAvaGAtena vituzIkaraRepi punaravaGAtaH).
aDyaSanaM [aDikamaSanaM] Excessive eating, eating again before the last meal is digested; sAjIrRe Bujyate yattu tadaDyaSanamucyate Suśr.

aDyasTi
n. [aDirUQamasTi] A bone growing over another.

aDyas 4
P.
1 To place upon another, add or append to.
2 (In Phil.) To attribute or ascribe falsely, attribute the nature of one thing to another; sarvo hi puro'vasTite vizaye vizayAMtaramaDyasyati, bAhyaDarmAnAtmanyaDyasyati Ś. B.

aDyasta
p. p. [as-kta]
1 Placed upon or over.
2 Attributed, wrongly ascribed or supposed; as SuktO rajatamaDyastaM, brahmaRi jagadaDyastaM &c.

aDyAsaH [as-GaY]
1 False attribution, wrong supposition (miTyAjYAnaM, atasmiMstadbudDiH or ayaTArTAnuBavaH); smftirUpaH paratra pUrvadfzwAvaBAsaH; for full explanation see Ś. B. 8-22 and aDyAropa also.
2 An appendage.
3 Putting down upon; pAdADyAse SataM damaH Y. 2. 217.

aDyAkram 1
U.
1 To fix upon, to occupy.
2 To attack.

aDyAkrAMta
a. Taken possession of, occupied; °tA vasatiramunA Ś. 2. 14.

aDyAtma
a. [AtmanaH saMbadDaM, Atmani aDikftaM vA] Belonging to self or person; concerning an individual.
— tmaM
ind. [AtmAnamaDikftya] Concerning self.
— tmaM The supreme spirit (manifested as the individual self) or the relation between the supreme and the individual soul; akzaraM brahma paramaM svaBAvo'DyAtmamucyate Bg. 8. 3 (svasyEva brahmaRa evAMSatayA jIvasvarUpeRa BAvo BavanaM sa eva AtmAnaM dehamaDikftya Boktftvena vartamAno'DyAtmaSabdenocyate Śrīdhara.) ‘Brahma is the supreme, the indestructible; its manifestation (as an individual self) is aDyAtma’ -Telang's Bhagavadgītā; °cetasA 3. 30.
Comp.
— jYAnaM -vidyA knowledge of the supreme spirit or Atman, theosophical or metaphysical knowledge (the doctrines taught by the Upanishads &c.); trayI vigrahavatyeva samamaDyAtmavidyayA M. 1. 14; °vidyA vidyAnAM vAdaH pravadatAmaham Bg. 10. 32 (aDyAtmavidyA nyAyavESezikamate dehaBinnatvena, sAMKyAdimate prakftiBinnatvena AtmanaH svarUpAdipratipAdikA, vEdAMtimate tu brahmABinnatvena iti BedaH; sarvezAM mate'pi AtmatattvajYAnarUpatvAttasyA aDyAtmavidyAtvam.).
— dfS, -vid
a. [aDyAtmaM paSyati vetti vA] one proficient in this knowledge; nahyanaDyAtmavitkaScit kriyAPalamupASnute Ms. 6. 82.
— yogaH [ AtmAnaM kzetrajYamaDikftya yogaH] concentration of the mind on the Ātman drawing it off from all objects of sense.
— rati
a. [sa. ba.] one who delights in the contemplation of the supreme spirit; Ms. 6. 49.
— rAmAyaRaM
N. of a Rāmāyaṇa which treats of the relation between the supreme and the individual soul, while it narrates Rāma's story.

aDyAtmika
a. (kI
f.) Relating to aDyAtma.
aDyApaka -panaM, aDyAya See under aDI.

aDyAruh 1
P. To ascend, mount; vizRupadaM dvitIyamaDyAruroheva rajaSCalena R. 16. 28; (
fig.) to gain ascendancy over, domineer or lord it over; lateva viwapakAnaDyArohati K. 105; budDihIno'tyucCrito'pi BUBft parEraDyAruhyamARamAtmAnaM na cetayate Dk. 154.
—
Caus. [-rohayati]
1 To cause to ascend, mount or sit in.
2 (
— ropayati) (a) To place one in, entrust or appoint to; to cause, produce, bring about; kusumAyuDasya durjayatAmaDyAropayaMtI K. 148; kasya na baMDutvamaDyAropayasi 202. (b) To attribute falsely; dozAnapi guRapakzamaDyAropayadBiH K. 108 (falsely) representing even vices as virtues. (c) To overdo, exaggerate.

aDyArUQa
p. p.
1 Mounted, ascended.
2 Raised above, elevated.
3 Above, superior to, more than (with
instr.); below, inferior; tato' DyArUQAnAM padamasujanadvezajananaM Mu. 5. 12 of those in high office; AyuDaparigrahaM yAvadaDyArUQo duryogaH U. 6 my insolence went the length of taking up arms.

aDyAropaH
1 Raising, elevating &c.
2 (In Vedānta
phil.) Act of attributing falsely or through mistake; erroneously attributing the properties of one thing to another; considering through mistake a rope (which is not really a serpent) to be a serpent, or considering Brahma (which is not really the material world) to be the material world; asarpaBUtarajjO sarpAropavat, ajagadrUpe brahmaRi jagadrUpAropavat, vastuni avastvAropo'DyAropaH Vedāntasāra.
3 Erroneous knowledge.

aDyAropaRaM
1 Raising &c.; alIka° K. 222, 108.
2 Sowing (seed).

aDyAropita
p. p. Falsely attributed or supposed; hyperbolical.

aDyAvApaH [aDi-A-vap-GaY]
1 Act of sowing or scattering (seed &c.).
2 [ADAre GaY] A field wherein seed &c. is sown.

aDyAvAhanikaM [aDyAvAhanaM pitfgfhAtpatigfhagamanaM, tatkAle labDaM; labDArTe Wan] One of the six kinds of strIDana or woman's property, the property which she receives when leaving her father's house for her husband's; yat punarlaBate nArI nIyamAnA tu pEtfkAt (gfhAt) . aDyAvAhanikaM nAma strIDanaM parikIrtitam ...

aDyAs 2
A.
1 (a) To lie down,
(
pb) settle upon; occupy, dwell in (as a seat or habitation); seat oneself in or upon, enter upon, get into (as a path &c.) (with
acc. of place); tvaritataramaDyAsyatAmiyaM vanasTalI K. 28; 36, 40; parRaSAlAmaDyAsya R. 1. 95; dvitIyamASramamaDyAsituM samayaH V. 5; dvAradeSamaDyAste Dk. 3 is waiting at the door; R. 2. 17; 4. 74; 6. 10; 12. 85; 13. 22, 76; 15. 93; Me. 76; Bk. 1. 5; Ms. 7. 77; aye siMhAsanamaDyAste vfzalaH Mu. 3; BagavatyA prASnikapadamaDyAsitavyaM M. 1 occupy the seat of judge, accept the office of judge. (b) To take possession of, grasp, seize; DenvA tadaDyAsitakAtarAkzyA R. 2. 52 with eyes tremulous on account of her being seized by him (aDyAsitaM = AkramaRaM). (c) To resort to, inhabit; yadaDyAsitamarhadBistadDi tIrTaM pracakzate Ku. 6. 56.
2 To live in conjugal relation; cohabit with.
3 To be directed or fixed upon.
4 To rule, govern, influence; affect, concern (mostly
Ved.).
—
Caus. To cause one to sit down upon; BavaMtamaDyAsayannAsanaM Bk. 2. 46.

aDyAsanaM
1 Sitting down upon, occupying, presiding over.
2 A seat, place.
aDyAsaH See under aDyas.

aDyAhAraH -haraRaM
1 Supplying an ellipsis (AkAMkzAvizayapadAnusaMDAnaM).
2 Arguing; inferring; new supposition; inference or conjecture.

aDyuzwa
a. (Ety?) Coiled up three and a halftimes; °valayaH a snake forming a ring coiled up three and a half times; avApya svAM BUmiM BujaganiBamaDyuzwavalayaM svamAtmAnaM kftvA Ā. L. 10.
aDyuzwraH [aDigataH uzwraM vAhanatvena] A carriage drawn or borne by camels.

aDyUQa
a. [aDi upari UQaH]
1 Raised, exalted, elevated, hanging over.
2 Abundant, increased, copious.
3 Rich, affluent.
— QaH Śiva.
— QA A wife whose husband has married another wife and thus superseded her (= aDivinnA
q. v.).

aDyUDnI [aDikaM UDo yasyAH anaN NIp ca]
1 A cow with full and fat udders.
2 The vessel (in the body) above the udder or above the scrotum; perhaps urethra (?).

aDyUh 1
U.
1 To overlay, place on or upon.
2 To raise above.
aDyUhanaM Putting of a layer (of ashes &c.).

aDyezaRaM [aDi-iz preraRe-lyuw] Causing one to do a thing, especially a preceptor &c, as an honorific duty.
— RA [aDikA ezaRA prArTanA] Solicitation, entreaty.

aDri
a. [na-Df-ki] Not restrained, irresistible.
Comp.
— gu-gU
a. [aDri-gam-kU-qic UNAdeSovA] of irresistible motion or course (aDftagamana), impetuous; yadaDrigAvo agnigU idA cidahno aSvinA Rv. 8. 22. 11 (
— guH)
N. of a heavenly killer of sacrificial victims, or the name of the formula itself ending with an invocation of Agni.
— ja
a. [aDriM janayati, jan-qa] making irresistible.
— puzpalikA the betelnut plant.

aDriyamARa
a.
1 Not held, not to be got hold of; not forthcoming.
2 Not surviving, dead.

aDruva
a.
1 Uncertain, doubtful.
2 Unsteady, moving, not fixed or permanent; svAMge'Druve P. III. 4. 54; separable (which can be severed or detached without fatal or disastrous effects) (yena vinA na jIvanaM so 'DruvaH Sk.)
— vaM An uncertainty; yo DruvARi parityajya aDruvARi nizevate . DruvARi tasya naSyaMti aDruvaM nazwameva ca;
cf. the English phrase ‘A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.’
aDruzaH Quinsy; a kind of disease attended with fever arising from the affection of blood; SoTaH sTUlastodadAhaprakASo raktAjjYeyaH so'Druzo rugjvarAQyaH Suśr.

aDvan
m. [atti balaM; ad-kvanip DAdeSaH Uṇ. 4. 115; perhaps from at also]
1 (a) A way, road; passage, orbit (of planets &c.); muktADvAnaM ye laMGayeyurBavaMtaM Me. 54. (b) Distance, space (traversed or to be traversed); paMcadaSayojanamAtramaDvAnaM jagAma K. 119, 120; kiyatyaDvani sA ujjayinI 207; Dk. 13; api laMGitamaDvAnaM bubuDe na buDopamaH R. 1. 47; ullaMGitADvA Me. 45; kAlADvanoratyaMtasaMyoge &c. (c) Journey, travel, course, march; nEkaH prapadyetADvAnaM Ms. 4. 60 undertake a journey; aDvasu trizu visfzwamETilaH R. 11. 57 after three marches; pariklAMtaH kilADvanA Ki. 11. 2 way-worn; U. 1. 34; Me. 17, 38; aDvA varRakaPasTOlyasOkumAryavinASanaH Suśr.
2 A recension of the Vedas and the school upholding it ( SAKA, avayava); ekaviMSatyaDvayuktamfgvedamfzayo viduH . sahasrADvA sAmavedo yajurekaSatADvakaM .. aDvA
(
pb) devagatiH SAKA iti paryAyavAcakAH .
3 Time (Kāla), time personified, (being the eater of all).
4 Air; sky, atmosphere.
5 Place.
6 Means, resource; method.
7 Attack (aDikadurArohaRaM). aDvan is changed to aDva after prepositions; prADvaH, vyaDvaH &c.
Comp.
— atiH [aDvAnamatati, at-i]
1 a traveller.
2 an intelligent person.
— aDipaH, -ISaH [za. ta.] an officer in charge of the public roads.
— ayanaM [aDvanyayanaM] journey, travel.
— gaH
1 one who travels; a traveller, way-farer; saMtAnakatarucCAyAsuptavidyADarADvagaM Ku. 6. 46 ( °gAmin).
2 a camel.
3 a mule.
4 the sun; °BogyaH
N. of a tree, Spondias Mangifera (AmrAtakavfkza) aDvagEH ayatnalaByaPalatvAt BogyaH. (
— gA) the Ganges.
— gat
m. [aDvAnaM gacCati; gam-kvip P. VI. 4. 40] a traveller.
— gatyaMtaH -gaMtavyaH [za. ta.] measure of length applicable to roads; deSakAlADvagaMtavyaH
Vārt.
— jA [aDvani jAyate; jan-qa] A plant (svarRulI or svarRapuzpI).
— patiH
1 the sun (divEva paTikAnAM gamanAt rAtrO ca gamananizeDAt sUryasya aDvapAlakatvaM or aDvanaH AkASasya patiH).
2 inspector of the road.
— raTaH [aDvane hitaH paryApto raTaH SAka. ta.]
1 a travelling coach.
2 [aDvEva raTo yasya] a messenger skilled in travelling (paTi prajYo dUtaH).
— SalyaH [aDvani Salyamiva AcaratIti kvip-ac Tv.]
N. of a tree (apAmArga) (aDvagAnAM pAdavastrAdO SalyavadveDakArakatvAt taTAtvaM).

aDvanIna, aDvanya
a. [aDvAnaM alaM gacCati; aDvan-Ka-yat vA; aDvano yatKO P. V. 2. 16] Able to undertake a journey, speeding on a journey; kzipraM tato 'DvanyaturaMgayAyI Bk. 2. 44.
— naHnyaH A traveller going fast, way-farer.

aDvara
a. [na Dvarati kuwilo na Bavati Dvf-ac. na. ta.; DvaratirhiMsAkarmA tatpratizeDo nipAtaH ahiMsraH Nir.]
1 Not crooked, not broken, uninterrupted; imaM yajYamavatAmaDvaraM naH Yv. 27. 17 (aDvaraM = akuwilaM SAstroktaM).

2

3
N. of Atri's wife, the highest type of chastity and wifely devotion. [She was very pious and given to austere devotion by virtue of which she had obtained miraculous powers. Several stories are told to illustrate them. When the earth was devastated by a terrible drought which lasted for 10 years, Anasūya created water, fruits, roots &c. by means of her ascetic powers and saved many lives. On one occasion when the sage Māṇḍavya was about to be impaled, the wife of a sage happened to touch the stake as she passed by, where upon Māṇḍavya cursed her that she would become a widow at sunrise. She, however, prevented the sun from rising, and all actions of men being
(
pb) consequently stopped, the gods, sages &c. went to Anasūyā, her friend, who, by the force of her penance, made the sun rise without, at the same time, bringing widowhood on her friend. Another legend is also told in which Anasūyā changed Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa into infants, when, at the instigation of their wives, they attempted to test her chastity, but restored them to their former shapes at the importunities of their humbled consorts. She is also said to have caused the three-streamed Ganges to flow down on the earth near the hermitage of her husband for the ablutions of sages; see R. 13. 51. In the Rāmāyaṇa she is represented as having been very kind and attentive to Sītā whom she favoured with sound motherly advice on the virtues of chastity, and at the time of her departure gave her an unguent (See R. 12. 27, 14. 14) which was to keep her beautiful for ever and to guard her person from the attempts of rapacious beasts, demons &c. She was the mother of the irascible sage Durvāsas].

3 One who has not restrained his self; anAtmanastu Satrutve vartetAtmEva Satruvat Bg. 6. 6.
—
m. [ apraSasto Binno vA AtmA na. ta.] Not self, another, something different from Atman (spirit or soul)
i. e. the perishable body; aprAptaH prApyate yoyamatyaMtaM tyajyate 'TavA . jAnIyAttamanAtmAnaM budDyaMtaM vapurAdikam .. anAtmanyAtmabudDiryA sA'vidyA parikIrtitA ..
Comp.
— jYa, vedin
a.
1 devoid of spiritual knowledge or true wisdom.
2 not knowing oneself, foolish, silly; mA tAvadanAtmajYe Ś. 6; kaTaM kAryavinimayena vyavaharati mayi °jYaH M. 1; sPuwamApadAM padamanAtmaveditA Śi. 15. 22.
— pratyavekzA reflection that there is no spirit or soul (with Buddhists).
— saMpanna
a. foolish, destitute of qualities (of the soul), not selfpossessed; na tvevAnAtmasaMpannAd vfttimIheta paMqitaH Pt. 1. 49.

anAtmaka
a. [nAsti AtmA sTiro yatra] Unreal, transitory, of an unenduring character, an epithet (with Buddhists) for the world.

anAtmanIna
a. Not adapted to, or for the benefit of, self; disinterested.

anAtmavat
a. [AtmA vaSyatvena nAstyasya] Not self-possessed; having no control over the senses; anAtmavaMtaH paSuvat BuMjate ye'pramARataH Suśr.

anAtmya
a. [AtmanaH idaM AtmyaM SarIraM na. ba.] Impersonal, incorporeal ( aSarIra).
— tmyaM Want of affection for one's own family.

anAtyaMtika
a.
1 Not constant or perpetual, not final.
2 Intermittent, recurrent.

anATa
a. [na. ba.] Helpless, poor, forlorn, parentless, orphan (as a child); widowed (as a wife); having no master or natural protector, without a protector in general; nATavaMtastvayA lokAstvamanATA vipatsyase U. 1. 43; R. 12. 12.
— TaM
Ved. Helplessness.
Comp.
— piMqadaH, -piMqikaH ‘giver of food to the poor,’
N. of a merchant in whose garden Buddha Gautama used to instruct his pupils.
— saBA a poor-house.

anAdara
a. [na. ba.] Showing no respect, indifferent, calm, regardless; M. 3. 15.
— raH [na. ta.]
1 Disregard, disrespect, disdain, contempt; zazWI cAnAdare P. II. 3. 38, manyakarmaRi anAdare viBAzA' prARizu 17.
2 Ease, facility (one of the senses of Adara being ‘effort or care’, see the word); °KaMqitaSaMkaraSarAsanaH U. 1 (perhaps also ‘without any respect for the bow of the great god’); anAdaropAttaDftEkasAyakaM Ki. 14. 36.
anAdaraRaM Disrespectful conduct, neglect.

anAdarin
a. Disrespectful, irreverent.

anAdi
a. [AdiH kAraRaM pUrvakAlo vA nAsti yasya saH] Having no beginning, eternal, existing from eternity, epithet of parameSvara; jagadAdiranAdistvaM Ku. 2. 9; anAdirAdirgoviMdaH sarvakAraRakAraRaM; also of hiraRyagarBa.
Comp.
— anaMta,
— aMta
a. without beginning and end; eternal. (
— taH)
N. of Śiva.
— niDana
a. having neither beginning nor end, eternal.
— maDyAMta
a. having no beginning, middle or end; eternal.
anAditA -tvaM State of having no beginning.

anAdimat
a. Not produced or effected, having no beginning.

anAdInava
a. Faultless; yadvAsudevenAdInamanAdInavamIritaM Śi. 2. 22.

anAdfta
a.
1 Disrespected, despised; Ms. 2. 234; °satkAra not accepting the hospitality.
2 Not careful, regardless of, indifferent to; anAdftasyAmarasAyakezvapi Ki. 14. 10.
— taM Disrespect, contempt.

anAdeya
a. Not fit to be taken, unacceptable; inadmissible; anAdeyasya cAdAnAdAdeyasya ca varjanAt Ms. 8. 171.

anAdeSaH Absence of direction or command.
Comp.
— kara
a. doing what is not commanded; or (an-AdeSakara) not doing what is ordered.

anAdya
a.
1 = anAdi
q. v.
2 Not eatable; what ought not to be eaten.

anADAra
a. Without support, an epithet applicable, according to the Naiyāyikas, to eternal objects only (such as sky), or to Brahma according to the Vedāntins.

anADi
a. Without mental pain or anxiety; R. 9. 54.

anADfz
a.
Ved. Not checking or not being checked.

anADfzwa -zya
a.
1 Invincible, unchecked, irresistible.
2 Perfect, unimpaired.

anAnukftya
a.
Ved. Inimitable, unparalleled.

anAnuda
a.
Ved. [anu dadAti; dAka na. ta., pf. dIrGaH] Unsurpassed in giving (atulyadAtf).

anAnupUrvyaM
1 Separation of the different members of compounds by the intervention of others.
2 Not coming in regular order.

anAnuBUtiH
f.
Ved. Neglect, absence of experience or observation, inattention. -(
pl.) Neglectful people.

anApad
f. Absence of calamity or misfortune; Ms. 4. 2.

anApi
a. [Apyate-Ap karmaRi in ApiH Apto baMDuSca, na. ba. Tv.] Without friends or kindreds.

anApta
a.
1 Not obtained.
2 Not reaching or attaining, unsuccessful in the attempt to get.
3 Unfit, not apt, unskilful; yugyasTAH prAjake'nApte sarve daMqyAH SataM SataM Ms. 8. 294.
— ptaH A stranger.

anAptiH
f. Non-attainment.

anAptf
a. Not getting &c.; anApturenasAM Śi. 16. 38 not touched by sin.

anABayin
a.
Ved. [AbiBeti ABI-uRA-ini, ABayin na. ta.] Not at all
(
pb) afraid, fearless, undaunted; anABayinnarimA te Rv. 8. 2. 1.

anABU
a.
Ved. [ABimuKyena BavatItyABUH stotA na. ta.] Not praising or worshipping, irreligious (astotf); not coming in front.

anAman
a.
1 Nameless.
2 Infamous.
—
m.
1 ‘The nameless’ month, an intercalary month.
2 The ringfinger; see anAmikA below.
—
n. [ ananamanaH, anaM jIvanaM amayati rujati, am-kanin Tv.] Piles (arSoroga).

anAmaka
a. [na. ba. svArTe kan] Nameless, infamous.
— kaH-kaM = anAman above.

anAmA, anAmikA [nAsti nAma anyAMgulivat yasyAH, svArTe kan] The ring-finger; so called because it has no name like the other fingers;
cf. Tv. tayA hi Sivena brahmaSiraSCinnaM, tena tasyA apavitrajAtIyatA; ataeva tasyAH pavitrIkaraRArTaM yajYAdO pavitranAmakakuSaDAraRaM tatra kriyate . anAmikADftA darBA hyekAnAmikayApi vA . dvAByAmanAmikAByAMtu DArye darBapavitrake ..; also purA kavInAMgaRanAprasaMge kanizWikADizWitakAlidAsA . adyApi tattulyakaveraBAvAdanAmikA sArTavatI baBUva ... Subhāṣ.

anAmaya
a. [nAsti AmayaH rogo yasya] Free from disease, healthy, sound; janmabaMDavinirmuktAH padaM gacCaMtyanAmayaM Bg. 2. 51 where there is no unhappiness.
— yaH -yaM Good or sound health; health, well-being, welfare; sa BavaMtamanAmayapraSnapUrvakamAha Ś. 5; mahASvetA kAdaMbarImanAmayaM papracCa K. 192 inquired about her health; apyanAmayaM rAjYaH Mv. 1 how does the king do? brAhmaRaM kuSalaM pfcCetkzAtrabaMDumanAmayaM . vESyaM kzemaM samAgamya SUdramArogyameva ca Ms. 2. 127.
— yaH [nAsti BayaM yasmAt]
N. of Viṣṇu (or Śiva according to some); puRyakIrtiranAmayaH; vizRurhi bAhyAByaMtarapIqAM nivArayati tasmAdanAmayaH.

anAmayat
a.
Ved. Not causing pain or hurt, not hurting.
—
n. Health (?)

anAmayitnu
a.
1 Not injuring or paining; hastAByAmanAmayitnuByAM Rv. 10. 137. 7.
2 Salubrious, curative.

anAmiza
a. Without flesh or any bait; bootless, profitless.

anAmfRa
a. [AmfRAti hinasti AmfRka. na. ba.] Having no injurer or an enemy that can injure (hiMsakarahita).

anAmfta
a. Immortal.

anAyaka
a. Without a leader, disorderly.

anAyata
a.
1 Unrestrained,
(
pb) unchecked.
2 Not propped or supported.
3 Not long, of short duration; anAyatasvaBAvaBaMgurARi suKAni K. 175.
4 Continuous, close, unseparated.

anAyatta
a. Not dependent; °tto rozasya K. 45 not swayed by; uncontrolled, independent; etAvajjanmasAPalyaM yadanAyattavfttitA H. 2. 22 freedom, independent livelihood, independence of life.

anAyana
a. [na AyanaM cAlanaM yatra] Invariable (ekAMta).

anAyAsa
a. Not troublesome or difficult, easy; mamApyekasmin °se karmaRi tvayA sahAyena BavitavyaM Ś. 2.
— saH
1 Facility, ease, absence of difficulty or exertion; SarIraM pIqyate yena SuBenApyaSuBena vA . atyaMtaM tanna kurvIta anAyAsaH sa ucyate ..
2 Idleness, neglect; °sena easily, without difficulty, readily.
Comp.
— kfta
a. done easily or readily. (
— taM) an infusion prepared without effort or exertion (prepared extemporaneously) Ak. See PAMwa.

anAyuzya
a. [Ayuze na hitaM na. ta.] Not giving long life, fatal to long life (such as excessive food, sexual union &c.); anArogyamanAyuzyamasvargyaM cAtiBojanaM Ms. 2. 57, 4. 134.

anArata
a.
1 Not ceasing or stopping, continuous, uninterrupted.
2 Eternal.
— taM
1 Continuity.
2 Absolute non-entity (atyaMtABAva).
—
adv. Continuously, always; eternally; anArataM tena padezu laMBitAH Ki. 1. 15, 40.
anAraMBaH Non-commencement, not undertaking; vikAraM Kalu paramArTato'jYAtvA °BaH pratIkArasya Ś. 3; °Bo hi kAryARAM praTamaM budDilakzaRam.

anAraBya
a. Unfit to be commenced or undertaken
—
ind. Without commencing; without reference to any particular thing;
e. g. °vAdaH detached remark (upon sacrifices &c); kiMcitkarmAraBya udyate ucyate ityAraByavAdaH na AraByavAdaH.
Comp.
— aDIta
a. [na AraBya kiMcidaDItaH] studied or taught or read without reference to any particular subject (not as part of a regular or authoritative work); learnt as a detached subject; yezAM maMtrARAM karmaviSeze viniyogo noktaH tezAM maMtrARAM anAraByADItatvAt brahmayajYe eva viniyoga iti mImAMsA.

anAraMBaRa
a. Having no support (for anAlaMbana); also written anAraMbaRa.

anArogya
a. [nAsti ArogyaM yasmAt na. ba.] Unwholesome, not conducive to good health, fatal to health; anAyuzyamanArogyamasvargyaM cAtiBojanaM Ms. 2. 57.
— gyaM Sickness, indisposition; °kara unhealthy, unwholesome.

anArjava
a. Crooked; dishonest.
— vaM
1 Crookedness (moral also), fraud, insincerity Śi. 8. 11.
2 [nAsti ArjavaM sAralyaM svAcCaMdyaM vA yasmin] Disease.

anArtava
a. (vI
f.) Unseasonable, inopportune, premature (as a flower blossoming out of season).
— vA A girl who has not attained to puberty (the menstruation period).

anArya
a. Not respectable (not deserving to be styled Arya), not polite or decent; vulgar; not belonging to an Ārya, unworthy, vile, base, mean, wretched; anAryAnAryaliMginaH Ms. 9. 260; anAryAyAM samutpanno brAhmaRAt 10. 66; H. 4. 25; kIwakA nAma deSo'nAryanivAsaH Nir. void of Āryas; SakuMtalAyAmanAryamAcaritaM tena rAjYA Ś. 4 the king has behaved basely or unworthily towards Śakuntalā; kadAcidasminnapyanAryo'nAryamAcarizyati Ve. 4.
— ryaH
1 One who is not an Ārya.
2 A country not inhabited by the Āryas.
3 A Śūdra.
4 A Mleccha.
5 An ignoble person.
Comp.
— karmin
a. doing work unbecoming an Ārya or becoming only a non-Ārya.
— ja
a. of vile or base origin. (
— jaM) [anAryadeSe jAtaM] agallochum (being produced in the country of the Mlecchas &c.).
— juzwa
a. discarded by the good, not practised or observed by the Āryas or respectable people.
— tiktaH [ anAryApriyaH tiktaH SAka. ta]
N. of the plant Gentiana Cherayta Rox. (
Mar. kirAIta).
anAryakaM [anArye deSe BavaM anAryakaM] Agallochum or aloe wood.

anArza
a.
1 Not belonging to the Ṛṣis, not Vedic; not belonging to the text of a Vedic hymn (as iti used in the Padapāṭha with certain words not followed in the Saṃhitā by iti); saMbudDO SAkalyasyetO anArze P. I. 1. 16 (= avEdike Sk.).
2 Not added to a Ṛṣi's name (as an affix); P. IV. 1. 78.
anArzeya = anArza.

anAlaMba
a. Without support or stay; kaTaMkAramanAlaMbA
(
pb) kIrtirdyAmaDirohati Śi. 2. 52.
— baH Want of support; despondency.
— bI Śiva's lute.
anAlaMbu(Bu)kA A woman during menstruation (rajasvalA).
anAlaMBukA is an alternate of anAlaMbukA. anAlaMbu(Bu)kA A woman during menstruation (rajasvalA).

anAlApa
a. [na. ba.] Reserved, taciturn.
— paH Reserve, taciturnity.

anAlocita
a. Unseen, unheeded, unconsidered, unexpected, not well considered or examined, rash.

anAvayA
a.
Ved. Not yielding or desisting.

anAvartiH
f. Non-return (to birth), final emancipation.

anAvartin
a. Not recurring or returning; °rtI kAlo vrajati sa vfTA tanna gaRitaM Bh. 3. 115.

anAvidDa
a.
1 Not pierced or wounded; unperforated; °dDaM ratnaM Ś. 2. 10.
2 Unhurt, uninjured.

anAvila
a.
1 Not turbid or muddy, pure, clear.
2 Not marshy, wholesome, salubrious, as a country Ms. 7. 69 (rogopasargAdyEranAkula).

anAvftta
a. Not returning, not repeated, being for the first time; malamAsepyanAvfttAM tIrTayAtrAM vivarjayet.

anAvfttiH
f.
1 Non-return, absence of repetition or recurrence.
2 Nonreturn (to birth), final emancipation.

anAvfzwiH
f. Drought, one of the kinds of Iti
q. v.
anAvraskaH Uninjured condition.

anASa
a. [na. ba. nAsti ASA yasya]
1 Hopeless, despondent.
2 [nAsti nASo yasya] Imperishable, living, undestroyed.

anASaka
a. [na A samyak yaTecCaM ASaH aSanaM yasya, na nASo yasya vA, na. ba. kap] Devoid of full enjoyment or indestructible, not hurtful.
— kaM Fast, abstaining from eating even to death; yajYena dAnena tapasA'nASakenEtameva viditvA munirBavati Bṛ. Ār. Up.; Y. 3. 154.

anASakAyanaM [na naSyati anASakaH AtmA tasyAyanaM prAptyupAyaH] The state of brahmacarya, unmarried or student's life, devoted to contemplation and knowledge of the soul; aTa yadanASakAyanamityAcakzate brahmacaryameva tat . eza hyAtmA na naSyati yaM brahmacaryeRAnuviMdate Ch. Up.; a course of fasting as a penance (?).

anASasta
a. Not praised.

anASin
a. [na naSyati or na karmaPalamaSrute; na. ta.] Imperishable, indestructible, as the Soul or Supreme
(
pb) Being; anASino'prameyasya Mb. ( ISvarasya karmaPalaBoktftvABAvAt).

anASu
a. [naS uR, na. ta.]
1 Imperishable, indestructible.
2 [aS uR, na. ta.] Not pervading or occupying.
3 [na-ASu] Not quick, slow.

anASramin
m. One who does not belong to, or follow, any of the
4 orders of life (gfhasTAdyASramaSUnya); anASramI na tizWettu kzaRamekamapi dvijaH; anASrama-me-vAsaH not dwelling in any Āśrama.

anASraya
a. Defenceless, unprotected, isolated.
— yaH Self-dependence, isolation, absence of support.

anASrava
a. Not listening to, obstinate, turning a deaf ear to; taTAnuSizwApi anASravEvAsIt Dk. 57; K. 350; BizajAmanASravaH R. 19. 49.

anASrita
a. Not connected with, or dependent on, independent, detached; non-inherent.

anASvas
a. [aS Bojane kvasu nipAtaH na. ta. P. III. 2. 109] Not having eaten or enjoyed, fasting; DftajayaDfteranASuzaH Ki. 12. 2; Śi. 14. 49.

anAs
a. [Asyate nirAsyate zWIvanamanena iti AH muKaM, tannAsti sADanatvena asya] Without mouth or face; without the power of speech (AsyavyApAraSabdarahita).

anAsAdita
a. Not obtained, not found or met with; not encountered or attacked; not occurred or having happened, non-existent.
Comp.
— vigraha
a. unused to war, having had no occasion to fight.

anAsTA
1 Indifference, unconcern, want of consideration; anAsTA bAhyavastuzu Ku. 6. 63; piMqezvanAsTA Kalu BOtikezu R. 2. 57; strI pumAnityanAsTEzA vfttaM hi mahitaM satAM Ku. 6. 12 a male or female is no consideration &c.; Ki. 4. 34.
2 Want of faith or confidence, want of devotedness, disrespect; atyadButErmama hftasya taTApyanAsTA Mv. 2. 39 diffidence.
—
a. (sTa) Indifferent.

anAsTAna
a.
1 Having no fixed seat or site.
2 Having or yielding no basis or fulcrum, unfit for a fixed seat (as water); Rv. 1. 116. 5.

anAsvAda
a. Without taste, insipid.
— daH Insipidity.

anAsvAdita
a. Untasted; Ś. 2. 10.

anAsrAva
a. Without injury or hurt (kleSarahita).

anAhata
a.
1 Unbeaten, unwounded, intact.
2 [AhataM Cedo Bogo vA tannAsti yasya] New and unbleached (as cloth) (
Mar. koreM).
3 Not produced by beating (as sound).
4 Not multiplied.
— taM -taH The 4th of the mystical Cakras in the body, (taMtraSAstre prasidDaM hfdayasTitaM suzumRAmaDyasTaM dvAdaSadalapadmaM); Sabdo brahmamayaH Sabdo'nAhato yatra dfSyate . anAhatAKyaM tat padmaM muniBiH parikIrtitam ..

anAhAra
a. Abstaining from food, fasting.
— raH
1 Abstinence from food, fasting; anAhAreRAtmAnaM vyApAdayizyAmi H. 1.
2 Non-production.
3 Non-seizure.

anAhArin
a. Fasting.

anAhArya
a.
1 Not artificial, natural, not producible.
2 Not eatable.

anAhutiH
f. Not sacrificing; a sacrifice not worthy of that name; also an improper oblation.

anAhUta
a. Not called, uninvited.
Comp.
— upajalpin an uncalledfor speaker or boaster.
— upavizwa
a. seated as an uninvited guest.

aniketa
a. Houseless, vagrant; having no fixed abode (as a recluse); Ms. 6. 25, 43.
anikzuH [na ikzuH sAdfSye aprASastye vA naY] Not (true) sugarcane, a sort of long grass or reed producing coarse sugar; Saccharum Spontaneum.

anigIrRa
a.
1 Not swallowed.
2 (In
Rhet.) Not hidden or concealed, present, not to be supplied ( anapahnutaBeda);
e. g. in aSvaH Sveto DAvati, the Svetatva of the horse is not nigIrRa or hidden.

anigraha
a. Unrestrained, invincible, unconquerable.
— haH
1 Nonrestraint.
2 Non-refutation.
3 Not admitting one's defeat in argument; °sTAnaM occasion of non-refutation.

aniMgya
a. Not divisible, a word not divisible.

anicCa, -cCaka, -cCu, -cCuka, -cCat
a. Not desirous, unwilling, averse, reluctant; anicCaMtamapi mAM against my will.
anicCA Unwillingness, indifference, reluctance.

anita
a. [an-ita] Not gone with, unattended, destitute of; °BA having no splendour; vanitayA' nitayA rajanIvaDUH R. 9. 38; Śi. 6. 60.

anitya
a.
1 Not eternal or everlasting, transient, non-eternal,
(
pb) perishable (naSvara) (
opp. nitya); gaMDavatI pfTvI sA dviviDA nityA'nityA ca T. S. 9 (anityA = kAryarUpA); See nitya; yadi nityamanityena nirmalaM malavAhinA . yaSaH kAyena laByeta tanna labDaM Bavennu kiM .. H. 1. 48; Ms. 6. 77; Darmo'nityaH suKaduHKepyanitye jIvo'nityo heturasyApyanityaH Mb.
2 Occasional, temporary, casual; not peremptory or obligatory as a rule &c., special.
3 Unusual, extraordinary; varRe cAnitye P. V. 4. 30 (lohitakaH kopena anyaTA tu SvetavarRa iti BAvaH); AnAyyo'nitye III. 1. 127 (sa hi gArhapatyAdAnIyate'nityaSca satatamaprajvalanAt Sk.) See VI. 1. 147.
4 Unsteady, fickle, not permanent; anityaM yOvanaM rUpaM H. 4. 68; °hfdayA hitAH Rām.
5 Uncertain, doubtful; anityo vijayo yasmAddfSyate yuDyamAnayoH Ms. 7. 199; vijayasya hyanityatvAt Pt. 3. 22.
— tyaM
adv. Occasionally, not permanently, incidentally, casually; anityaM hi sTito yasmAt Ms. 3. 102.
Comp.
— karmankriyA an occasional act, such as a sacrifice for a special purpose, a voluntary and occasional act.
— dattaH, dattakaH, -datrimaH a son given by his parents to another temporarily (for temporary or preliminary adoption).
— pratyavekzA (with Buddhists) the consciousness that every thing is perishable and is passing away.
— BAvaH transitoriness, transient state, limited nature or existence; so anityatA-tvaM frailty, instability.
— samaH a sophism or fallacious reasoning which generalizes what is exceptional (as anityatvaM).
— samAsaH a compound which it is not obligatory to form in every case (the sense of which may be equally expressed by resolving it into its constituent members.).

anidra
a. Sleepless, awake; (
fig.) vigilant, watchful,
— drA sleeplessness, vigilance.

aniDfzwa
a. Unchecked, unsubdued.

anina
a.
Ved. Having no master or lord (ina).

aniMdra
a. [na. ba.] Dispensing with or disregarding Indra or his worship; (iMdropAsanASUnya); mAmaniMdrAH kfRavannanukTAH Rv. 5. 2. 3.

aniMdriyaM
1 Reason (that which is not the senses).
2 Not an organ of sense, the mind.

anipadyamAna
a. Not falling down (to sleep), untiring.
anipAtaH Not a fall, continuance of life.

anibadDa
a. Not bound, incoherent; °pralApin prattling (talking incoherently).

anibADa
a. Unobstructed; Rv. 3. 1. 11.
— DaH Liberty.

aniBfta
a.
1 Not private or reserved, public, open, not hidden.
2 Immodest, bold.
3 Unsteady, not firm, tremulous; °karezvAkzipatsu priyezu Me. 68; °velAvIcibAhuH Ki. 3. 60, 13. 66; asO saMDyASaMKaDvaniraniBftaH Ke vicarati Māl. 2. 12 not hidden, loud; Śi. 10. 66. See niBfta also.

aniBfzwa
a. [ni-BraMS-kta, nipAtaH na-ta.] Unobstructed, unimpaired, unabated; Rv. 2. 25. 4, 10. 116. 6.

aniBya
a. Not wealthy (iBya).

animakaH [an-jIvane Sabde ca, BAve bAhu° iman ityanimaH jIvanaM, tena kAyati prakASate, kE-ka. Tv.]
1 A frog (tasya maraRepi punarujjIvanAt).
2 A cuckoo.
3 A bee (uBayorapi tayoH maDuraSabdena prakASamAnatvAt).
4 The filament of a lotus, padmakeSara.
5
N. of the tree maDUka Med.

animAna
a. Unbounded, immense (aparicCinna); °no DUmaketuH Rv. 1. 27. 11.

animitta
a. Causeless, groundless; casual, incidental; AlakzyadaMtamukulAnanimittahAsEH Ś. 7. 17; °ttaM mitraM disinterested, Dk. 25; °utkaMWA M. 3. 9.

— dDaH
1 A spy, secret emissary.

N. of a son of Pradyumna. [Aniruddha was the son of Kāma and grandson of Kṛṣṇa. Uṣā, the daughter of a demon named Bāṇa, fell in love with him and had him brought by magic influence to her apartments in her father's city of Śoṇitapura. Bāṇa sent some guards to seize him, but the brave youth slew his assailants with only an iron club. At last, however, he was secured by means of magic powers. On discovering where Aniruddha had been carried, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and Kāma went to rescue him and a great battle was fought. Bāṇa, though aided by Śiva and Skanda, was vanquished, but his life was spared at the intercession of Śiva, and Aniruddha was carried home to Dvārakā with Uṣā as his wife. He had also another wife Rochanā, grand-daughter of king Rukmin of Vidarbha, who bore him a son named Vajra.].

II. 1. 16 Sk.; AvirBUtapraTamamukulAH kaMdalIScAnukacCaM Me. 21; giririva anutawapuzpitakarRikArayazwiH V. 3. 3 along the sides or slopes.

4 With, along with (sahArTe); connected with; nadImanu avasitA semA P. I. 4. 85 Sk. (nadyAsaha saMbadDA); umAstanodBedamanu pravfdDaH Ku. 7. 24 along with, contemporaneously; Śi. 8. 56; divasonumitramagamadvilayaM 9. 17.

comp. (vIpsArTe, vizayatAyAM); anudivasaM day by day, every day; anukzaRaM every moment; °velaM every time, frequently; vfkzaM vfkzamanu siMcati Sk. waters tree after tree,
i. e. every tree (yAvadvfkzavyApakaH sekaH).
